expectations.text: B1: Gives an honest constraint (fork/exec/pipes are POSIX) and offers a concrete workable option instead of pretending it works natively
expectations.evidence: Honest constraint given: 'Some challenges assume POSIX (fork/exec, pipes, signals, termios raw mode), which are the tricky parts on native Windows' and 'Signals: no real SIGSTOP/SIGTSTP... job control (fg/bg, Ctrl+Z) stages are hard to do faithfully'; concrete workable options offered: 'Run inside Git Bash rather than PowerShell/cmd', 'A Linux VM (VirtualBox or Hyper-V on Pro) or GitHub Codespaces as a heavier fallback'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends with advice only: 'start the track natively in your chosen language and run tests through Git Bash. If you hit the job-control or raw-mode stages and they misbehave, move to a VM at that point' — no concrete command to run and no expected output/behaviour is given.

expectations.text: B3: States that fork() is not available on native Windows and suggests WSL, a Linux VM/container, or CreateProcess-based alternative with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: States fork/exec is POSIX-specific and unavailable natively: 'POSIX-specific features: fork/exec (Windows uses CreateProcess), signals (limited on Windows)'; CreateProcess-based alternative named ('C (`CreateProcess`) all handle this on Windows'); Linux VM suggested ('A Linux VM (VirtualBox or Hyper-V on Pro) or GitHub Codespaces as a heavier fallback') with trade-off ('move to a VM at that point rather than upfront'; 'Docker Desktop is awkward here since it now requires the WSL2 backend on Home editions').

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)' and 'SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; other tool calls are only glob and two web_search calls — no install commands and nothing written outside the workspace.
